title: [recoverability] Two backup keys, part A: dumps and bundles say the key that sealed them (SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY), verify and the restore drill read each with the key its record names, the first bundle under a new key is full
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 114 [recoverability]: two backup keys, part A (dumps, bundles, verify, the restore drill). Every new dump and bundle is sealed with the key SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY names, and says so. verify and the drill read each object with the key its record names. The first bundle under a new key is full, and a reader that lacks a key says which one.

Read sync/design-backup-two-keys.md revision 2 (rev-g PASS; cc-astra's read may add revisions) and, in crates/spawn-cli/src: backup.rs (Settings::from_env, with_r2, gpg_with, put_object, dump, bundle, bundle_records, verify, verify_bundle, restore_and_compare, record_verified) and backup/restore_drill.rs (restore_drill, chain_of, unrestorable, run, fetch_bundle).

Why. The owner's decision (lead-mac 10:01, point 2, made urgent at 10:08): a new key for every new backup, with the old key kept only to read existing bundles. Today one file (`backup.key`) seals everything, and no record says which key sealed it.

Required behaviour.
Key files.
- `<key dir>/backup.key.<name>`, mode 600. The key dir is `SPAWN_BACKUP_KEY_DIR`, default `~/.config/spawn`.
- A name matches `^k[1-9][0-9]*$`.
- k1's file is found in this order: `SPAWN_BACKUP_KEY_FILE` if set (it keeps its meaning, so 104.sh and check-j12 are unchanged); else `<key dir>/backup.key.k1`; else the old `<key dir>/backup.key`. A `mv` of backup.key to backup.key.k1 is therefore found.
- Every other key's file is only `<key dir>/backup.key.<name>`.

One place holds the default:
- `backup::key_name(named: Option<&str>) -> Result<name, String>`: None gives k1; a name of the right shape gives itself; anything else is refused with the rule alone, never the value: "is not a backup key name (k and a number from 1, as k2)". Each caller puts the source before it: "SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY", "the sealed_with of <backup.dumped or backup.bundled> record <event id>", or "the x-amz-meta-spawn-seal of <object key>". A value that is not a name can hold anything, a key's content included (cc-astra A53), so it is never printed or recorded.
- Every reader calls it: for a record's `sealed_with`, for an object's `x-amz-meta-spawn-seal`, and for SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY.

Sealing (dump and bundle).
- The sealing key is SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY (unset: k1). A value that is not a name, or a key whose file is missing or not 600, refuses the run: exit 2, recorded as today's refusals are (the record's skipped reason names SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY, or the file). It never falls back to k1.
- A dump's decrypt-back check uses the key it sealed with.
- `backup.dumped` and `backup.bundled` gain `"sealed_with": "<name>"`. Every object they PUT carries `x-amz-meta-spawn-seal: <name>`.
- The store's objects carry it too. `spawn store put` already seals with the sealing key's file (Settings::with_r2), so put_new_object (the store's PUT, and only the store's; dumps and bundles go through put_object) sends `x-amz-meta-spawn-seal: <SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY's name>`. This moves the store's header from the design's objective B into A (rev-e's N2 on 114, closed at the source). An object with no header still reads as k1 everywhere, so the header changes nothing for a reader of older objects. Opening a previous store manifest of another key, and the record's `sealed_with`, stay B's (objectives 115 and 116).
- bundle builds only on earlier records sealed with the sealing key (their names from key_name), in bundle() itself, after bundle_records. bundle_records is unchanged, because the drill and verify share it. So with no record of the new key yet, the bundle is full and its base_event_id null, whatever full bundle of another key this week holds; the next one is an increment on it.

Reading (verify and the drill). Settings::from_env stops requiring a key file. A reader needs a key's file only when it reaches a record sealed with that key.
- verify:
  - It reads the dump with the dump record's key and the bundle with the bundle record's. Each record's name is checked against its object's header (absent means k1 on both): when they differ, that half fails "record says <a>, object says <b>".
  - A missing key file fails that half with "the dump (or: the bundle) is sealed with <name>; its key file <path> is not on this host", and verify exits 1. <path> is the file the lookup would use; for k1 with SPAWN_BACKUP_KEY_FILE unset it is "<key dir>/backup.key.k1 (or backup.key)".
  - backup.verified gains `sealed_with` (the dump's) and `bundle.sealed_with` (the bundle's).
- restore-drill:
  - Every link of the chain must name the newest link's key. A chain that crosses keys is refused as broken: exit 1, "the backup cannot be restored: the chain crosses keys…".
  - A link whose sealed_with is not a name: exit 2, both resources recorded failed with reason exactly "the sealed_with of backup.bundled record <event id> is not a backup key name (k and a number from 1, as k2)".
  - The chain key's file missing: exit 2, both resources recorded failed with reason exactly "the bundle chain is sealed with <name>; its key file <path> is not on this host" (the path as above).
  - Each object's header is checked against the chain's key: when they differ, "record says <a>, object says <b>", as a backup that cannot be restored (exit 1).
  These records name the newest stored bundle, as unrestorable's do today.
- Only an accepted name is printed or recorded about a key. A value that is refused as a name is never echoed: the refusal names where it came from (the variable, the record's type and event id, or the object's key and header) and the rule. No key's content reaches an output, a record or an argv (gpg gets the file by path).

What stays: the store's reading (`spawn store`, backup/store.rs) is objective 116's. The store keeps sealing with the sealing key's file through Settings::with_r2, which still requires that file, mode 600. A bad SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY refuses there too and never seals with k1 in its place (a unit test pins it, rev-e's F1). Until 116 lands, a store whose last manifest is k1's cannot put under k2 (it opens that manifest with k2), so the store's drop-in setting k2 waits for 116. deploy/backup (README, lib.sh, pg-backup.sh) is protected: the README's manual-restore line and the scripts' default are the lead's change, made before the rename (design (4), N1). Landing this changes nothing on a host by itself: with SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY unset and only backup.key, everything seals with k1 exactly as today, and the records add `sealed_with: k1`. The switch is the lead's steps, after objective B lands.

Differences from the design text, for the reviewer:
- The design's table row `k7` gives "unknown backup key name". `k7` is a well-formed name, so here it gives the missing-file refusal (its file is not on the host). A value that is not a name is refused by its source and the rule, never by its value (the design's (4) table quotes the value; cc-astra A53, rev-g L1); the scenario uses a made-up secret-shaped value.
- The paths in the reasons are the real key dir, not a literal `~/.config/spawn`.

Unit tests (spawn-cli, made-up keys in scratch files, never HOME):
- key_name: absent gives k1; k2 and k12 give themselves; k0, K2, k2/.., "", k, k01 and a made-up key's content are errors, each the rule alone (the value in none of them).
- k1's lookup order: SPAWN_BACKUP_KEY_FILE, then backup.key.k1, then backup.key; any other name only backup.key.<name>.
- A record and a header that differ are refused.
- After the switch, the first bundle's earlier records are empty (so it is full) while a k1 full exists.
- The store's required sealing key: a bad name refuses, never k1's file; not required, k1's file stands in.
- The drill's chain key: one key; crossed keys refused; an unknown name refused by its record.
Each default and each refusal removed alone must fail a test or the scenario.

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs and crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs. One crate. Size, an exception decided by the lead (11-13): the throwaway adds 497 lines and removes 44 (code, doc comments and unit tests; R5's no-echo rule is about 55 of them). It stays whole: a split would put two open objectives on backup.rs, and its sealing half alone would let records say k2 before anything can read by record.

No polled read changes. The records are read by the backup runs themselves, and the Core lines card and alerts read the same fields as today.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/114.sh. It runs on its own database, scratch HOME, GNUPGHOME and key directory, against 104's local R2 stand-in, with made-up keys. k1 starts under the old name.
(1) Before the switch: a dump and a bundle exit 0, and their records and objects say k1. So does every object `spawn store put` stores, in a second stand-in whose bucket is the scenario's own work bucket (bb114-work) under a locktest/ prefix. Neither r2-store.env nor r2.env is read, and no call leaves the host.
(1b) In the switch runbook's window (backup.key.k2 made, backup.key still there, SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY unset): a dump exits 0, says k1 in its record and on its object, and decrypts with backup.key and not with backup.key.k2; a bundle exits 0 as an increment on (1)'s full bundle and says k1; verify exits 0 with sealed_with k1 and bundle.sealed_with k1. A build that seals with the newest key file present when the seal key is unset fails here.
(2) After the switch (the mv, SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY=k2): a dump says k2 in its record and on its object, and decrypts with k2 to its record's sha256, and not with k1. A store put under a fresh prefix stores objects that all say k2, and its manifest decrypts with k2 to a manifest, and not with k1.
(3) verify exits 0, with sealed_with k2 and bundle.sealed_with k1. With the dump's object header changed to k1 (its record k2), verify exits 1 with reason exactly "record says k2, object says k1"; with the bundle's changed to k2 (its record k1), "record says k1, object says k2".
(4) With k1's file away: verify exits 1 with the bundle reason; the drill exits 2 with both resources failed, reason exact. With k1 back and the k1 bundle's object stripped of its header (as every bundle stored before this objective is), the drill exits 0 and both resources pass.
(5) The first k2 bundle is full with no base despite this week's k1 full, says k2 and opens with k2 only; the next is an increment on it.
(6) With only k2 and SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY unset, the drill exits 0.
(7) With only k1: the drill exits 2, reason exact.
(8) With an object's header changed to k1 under a k2 record: the drill exits 1 with "record says k2, object says k1".
(9) With SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY set to a made-up secret-shaped value that is no name, and with =k3 (no file): the dump exits 2, stores nothing, and records the refusal ("SPAWN_BACKUP_SEAL_KEY is not a backup key name (k and a number from 1, as k2)", or backup.key.k3).
(10) A record whose sealed_with is that value: the drill exits 2, reason exact with the event id.
(11) No key's passphrase or R2 secret is in any output or record.
(12) The same value as an object's x-amz-meta-spawn-seal: verify exits 1 with the dump's reason exact ("the x-amz-meta-spawn-seal of <object key> is not a backup key name (k and a number from 1, as k2)"), and the drill exits 1 naming the bundle's object the same way. The value is in no output of any run and in no record but the one (10) planted.
104.sh must keep passing. check-tests.sh and check-clippy.sh must pass.
